title.narrative: Health System Strengthening for Human Capital Development in Eswatini

description.narrative: The objective of the Health System Strengthening for Human Capital Development in Eswatini Project for Eswatini is to improve the coverage and quality of key reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health (RMNCAH), nutrition and Noncommunicable Disease (NCD) services in Eswatini. The Project has four components. 1. Improve health service delivery to increase the coverage and quality of health services to build human capital component will improve health service delivery. Subcomponent 1.1. Build capacity of health care workers to deliver enhanced, high impact RMNCAH, and nutrition and NCD services across the continuum of care will support: (a) Competency-based and residential trainings for health care workers to deliver high-quality RMNCAH, nutrition, and NCD services across the continuum of care; (b) Technical Assistance (TA) and procurement of tablets/technology to develop, test, and scale up provider digital decision support tools for RMNCAH to consolidate the trainings and ensure that competencies of health care workers are maintained for enhanced decision making; (c) Specialist training and mentorship to operationalize a four-bed specialized neonatal unit; (d) Creation of a Community of Practice (CoP) for midwives to promote continuous professional development, intra-professional collaboration, and staff morale for improved maternal and neonatal outcomes. Subcomponent 1.2. Increase the availability of drugs, commodities, functioning equipment, and client data for high-quality health and nutrition service delivery in facilities will support: (a) Modernization and scale-up of an interoperable electronic record management system for service inputs and service delivery and coverage to strengthen evidence-based service planning and management; (b) Construction of an Integrated Operations Centre with upgraded fleet; (c) Limited procurement of key commodities and equipment for nutrition and NCDs; (d) Procurement of biomedical equipment and supplies for hygiene and sanitation to supplement COVID-19 health care readiness in hospitals and health facilities. Subcomponent 1.3. Strengthen the capacity of facilities, programs, and regions to monitor quality of care, supervise, and implement a Quality Management Approach in health facilities will ensure the delivery of high-quality services by strengthening the capacity of facilities, programs, and the Regional Health Management Teams (RHMTs) to supervise, monitor, and implement a Quality Management Approach (QMA) in health facilities. 2. Increase community demand for RMNCAH, nutrition and NCD services component will support: (a) Strengthening the Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) Program to conduct community sensitization and outreach; (b) Scale-up of social accountability monitoring of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services; (c) Targeted Social and Behavioral Change Communication (SBCC) and (d) Design, develop, and scale up client-based digital applications to help generate awareness, improve knowledge, and boost uptake of services and adherence to appointments and treatment. 3. 3. Strengthen the Ministry of Health (MOH's) stewardship capacity to manage essential health and nutrition services and project activities component will provide TA to support the drafting of updated regulations, policies, and strategies including for the draft Health Bill, professional regulatory bodies, National Quality of Care Framework, public-private partnerships, nutrition, sanitation, and health care waste management (HCWM)—including the capture or combustion of fugitive methane emissions—and health financing. 4. Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) will allow for rapid reallocation of project proceeds in the event of a future natural or manmade disaster or crisis that has caused or is likely to imminently cause a major adverse economic and/or social impact during the life of the project.

The project development objective is to improve the coverage and quality of key reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health (RMNCAH), nutrition and NCD services (hypertension and diabetes) in Eswatini.

title.narrative: Number of people receiving outpatient services

comment.narrative: This indicator was added at the time of the ICR to document the contribution of the Project to the new CRI on the number of people who received outpatient services. The number is calculated from CMIS. Please refer to Annex 5C for the methodology. Given that this indicator was added ex post, the target is indicative.

IRI 14 - Number of people reached with RMNCAH, nutrition and NCD- specific communication as part of targeted SBCC interventions

comment.narrative: IRI 14 was an original indicator with a baseline of 0 and a target of 82,000 mothers and adolescents. In the June restructuring, the target audience was expanded to include all people. The indicator was dropped in the June 2023 restructuring, as the MoH was unable to collect any data. The IRI 14 achievement rate is 0 for phase I of the project.

title.narrative: IRI 15 - Number of client-based digital application users

comment.narrative: IRI 15 was an original indicator with a baseline of 0 and a target of 41,000 users. In the June 2022 restructuring, the target was increased to 78,000. However, in the June 2023 restructuring, the indicator was dropped for lack of progress. The IRI 15 achievement rate is 0 for phase I of the project.

title.narrative: IRI 9 - Number of facilities using eLMIS for supply management

comment.narrative: IRI 9 was an original indicator with a baseline of 12 and a target of 20. The baseline was reset at 0, and the target was set at 22 in the June 2022 restructuring. The target was lowered in the 2023 restructuring (to 9) and dropped in the 2025 restructuring. For Phase I, the indicator is not achieved regardless of whether one uses the 2022 or 2023 targets: Achievement rate is 3/22=14% or 3/9=33%. For Phase II, IRI9 is included because it was dropped in the last 6 months only, when disbursement had already reached 89% of the final disbursed amount. The eLMIS was subsequently developed outside of the Project. The IRI 9 achievement rate is 3/9 = 33% for Phase II.

title.narrative: IRI 16 - Number of updated regulations, strategies, legal framework, and guidelines submitted

comment.narrative: IRI 16 was an original indicator with a baseline of 0 and a target of 4. In the June 2022 restructuring, the target was increased to 17, therefore the Phase I target is 17. The target was reduced twice in June 2023 (to 10) and in February 2025 (to 8). Given the late reduction in the final target, the ICR uses a Phase II target of 17. The IRI 16 achievement rate is 10/17 = 59 % for Phase I and 10/10 = 100% for Phase II. The indicator is achieved in Phase II independently of the choice of Phase II target.

title.narrative: IRI 8 - Number of HCWs trained on RMNCAH, nutrition and/or NCD services

comment.narrative: IRI 8 is an original indicator with a baseline of 0 and a target of 150. The target was increased three times to reach 1,100 in the February 2025 restructuring. The IRI 8 achievement rate is 1,429 / 1,100 = 130% for both phases.

title.narrative: IRI 13 - Number of community health workers (CHWs) including rural health motivators (RHMs) trained to conduct community sensitization & outreach on RMNCAH, Nutrition and NCD services

comment.narrative: IRI 13 was an original indicator with a baseline of 0 and a target of 5,000. In the June 2022 restructuring, the target was lowered to 2500; however, the target was subsequently increased to 3,000 in the June 2023 restructuring. The ICR uses a target of 3,000 for both phases. The IRI 13 achievement rate is 2908/3000 = 97% for both phases.

title.narrative: IRI 1 - People who have received essential health, nutrition, and population (HNP) services

comment.narrative: IRI 1 is an original indicator with a baseline of zero and a target of 107,882. The target was set as the sum of the targets for IRI 3 and IRI 4. The target changed to 294,360 in the June 2022 restructuring, as the underlying targets of IRI 03 and 04 also changed. The ICR uses the corrected targets for IRI 3 and 4 to update the target for IRI 1; the updated target is 428,008. The achievement on this indicator is the sum of the recalculated achievements on IRI 3 and 4, hence 428,966. The source of information is CMIS. The IRI 1 achievement rate is 428,966/428,008 = 100% for both phases.

title.narrative: IRI 1 - People who have received essential health, nutrition, and population (HNP) services

comment.narrative: IRI 1 is an original indicator with a baseline of zero and a target of 107,882. The target was set as the sum of the targets for IRI 3 and IRI 4. The target changed to 294,360 in the June 2022 restructuring, as the underlying targets of IRI 03 and 04 also changed. The ICR uses the corrected targets for IRI 3 and 4 to update the target for IRI 1; the updated target is 428,008. The achievement on this indicator is the sum of the recalculated achievements on IRI 3 and 4, hence 428,966. The source of information is CMIS. The IRI 1 achievement rate is 428,966/428,008 = 100% for both phases.

title.narrative: IRI 11 - Percentage of target health facilities that received at least one comprehensive quality assessment applying the appropriate checklist and protocol, and received adequate feedback from RHMT

comment.narrative: Original: BL=0, T=90%, complementing PDO5 (which has assessment outcomes). BL/T unchanged. Original denom. covered all 262 facilities. The 2022 restructuring introduced an incremental denominator, intended to rise annually to 262 by Project end. However, only 13 facilities received a comprehensive assessment by closing. The ISR final value used denominator=13, effectively setting numerator=denominator and yielding 100% achievement. The ICR corrects this by applying the same intermediate approach as PDO5, using a more realistic denom. of 52 facilities (excluding 203 very small clinics without maternities and 7 private hospitals), without reverting to 262. The numerator counts facilities assessed at least once over the project life. By Project end, 24 of 52 facilities (46%) had received a comprehensive quality assessment. IRI11 achievement = 24/52 = 46% (both phases).

title.narrative: PDOI 5 - Percentage of target health facilities that meet a minimum standard of quality as measured by a Health Facility Quality Index

comment.narrative: Original: BL=0, T=80%. T reduced to 70% in the 2022 restr.; unchanged in 2023 and 2025. Denominator was narrowly defined as # of targeted facilities assessed. Original targeted facilities # to be assessed was 262 , gradually reduced to 24 during supervision, substantially lowering the bar. At Project closure, assessment tool was developed and tested, but only 24 facilities had been assessed, of which 17 met minimum quality standard. For Phase I, achievement is (17/262)/80=8% against original %T and 262 facilities, and (17/52)/70=47% against the revised % T and intermediate # of facilities to be assessed. Phase I: not achieved independently of T choice. For Phase II, achievement is (17/52)/70=47% against the revised % T and intermediate # of facilities to be assessed (ie. not achieved) and (17/24)/70 = 110% against final target (ie. achieved). Overall Phase II achievement fell short of intent and therefore Phase II overall is partly achieved.

title.narrative: IRI 17 - Number of MOH management staff at national and regional level trained

comment.narrative: IRI 17 was an original indicator with a baseline of 0 and a target of 20. In the June 2022 restructuring, the target was increased to 64. Subsequently, the target was reduced twice in June 2023 (to 55) and in February 2025 (to 40). Given the late reduction in the final target, the ICR uses a target of 55 for Phase II. The IRI 17 achievement rate is 78/64 = 122 % for Phase I and 78/55 = 142% for Phase II. The indicator is achieved independently of the choice of target.

title.narrative: IRI 12 - Satisfaction rates of clients with the quality of health services

comment.narrative: IRI 12 was an original indicator with a baseline of 50 and a target of 75. The baseline was lowered to 0 in the June 2022 restructuring, though it is unclear why. The IRI 12 achievement rate is 900/75 = 120% for both phases.

title.narrative: IRI 18 - Percentage of target health facilities with at least one HCW sensitized on GBV guidelines

comment.narrative: IRI 18 was an original indicator with a baseline of 18 and a target of 43. In the June restructuring, the baseline was set to 0 and the target was set to 90. The denominator of the target for 2025 was 259 facilities. The ISRs report that 93% of target facilities had at least one HCW sensitized on GBV guidelines. The IRI 18 achievement rate is 93 / 90 = 103% for both phases.

title.narrative: IRI 6 - Number of people screened and diagnosed with hypertension

comment.narrative: IRI 6 was an original indicator with a BL of 22,160 and a T of 31,230. The T was increased twice to reach 40,000 in the June 2023 restructuring. The BL was updated to 22,624 in line with updated CMIS data. The BL, T, and reported numbers represent the # of people with a diagnosis of hypertension seen for any reason at outpatient departments in facilities connected to CMIS in year Y. This indicator does not represent screening (which is for patients not yet diagnosed) or new diagnoses (since both existing and new hypertension are included). Although the numbers therefore do not correspond to the original indicator label ("# of people screened and diagnoses with hypertension"), they are a useful gauge of ongoing access to primary health care services for patients with hypertension. The IRI 6 achievement rate is (50,242-22,624)/(40,000-22,624) = 159 % for both phases.

title.narrative: PDOI 2 - Percentage of children under 5 years of age provided with a basic package of nutrition specific services

comment.narrative: Original: BL=0, T=85. Restr. (2022): BL=32, T=55 with BL recalculated using CMIS data. For year Y, denom. is a statistical estimate of U5 cohort size. ISR reported numer. could not be replicated at ICR, so ICR used a new script to extract numer. from CMIS. Numer. is children receiving a growth monitoring visit & vitamin A in Y; for children born in June-Dec of Y, only growth monitoring is required, as vitamin A is not recommended <6 months. Recalculated BL values are 24 (2019) and 42 (2020); given the large gap, the ICR retains BL=32, which lies between these values. The indicator peaked at 62 in 2022, and declined thereafter. Final indicator value is 48. Achievement = (48–32)/(55–32)=70% (both phases).

title.narrative: PDOI 4 - Percentage of pregnant women receiving at least 4 ANC that meet defined quality standards

comment.narrative: Original: BL=0, T=60. Restr. (2022): BL=8.6, T=50 to align w/ observed data rather than reduce ambition; unchanged in 2023 and 2025 restr. ISR-reported values lacked cohort analysis to verify service receipt and counted ANC visits across multiple pregnancies to determine ANC4+. ICR recalculated indicator using a cohort approach: for year Y, denom. is all women delivering in Y; numer. is women delivering in year Y who received ANC4+ visits and urinalysis, BP measurement and Hb test within 38 weeks before delivery. 2025 results cover Jan–Dec. In this way, BL=4 (2020), which the ICR adopts. To preserve the BL–T delta of 41, the ICR uses an adjusted T=45 (instead of 50). Achievement = (19–4)/(45–4)=38% (both phases).

title.narrative: PDOI 1 - Percentage of patients diagnosed with hypertension and/or diabetes who are managed at the PHC level

comment.narrative: Original: BL=0, T=80. Restr. (2022): BL=58, T=90 to align w/ CMIS data. ISR reported definition & values could not be ascertained at ICR. The ICR therefore used a new script to extract the indicator from CMIS. Each patient's first diagnosed (dx) date is first visit tagged w/ hypertension (HT) or diabetes (DM) in 2020–25. For year Y, denom. is patients first diagnosed in Y (excluding prior years). For the 2020 BL only, denom. does not exclude patients with earlier dx. The numer. for Y includes patients newly diagnosed in Y who received =1 defined HT/DM service (labs or meds) at a PHC outpatient department within 90 days of first diagnosis. 90-day window matches quarterly ISR approach. 2025 results cover Jan–Dec. HT and DM patients may overlap in numer. and denom. In this way, ICR-computed BL=59 and end value=60. Indicator peaked at 64 (2021) & declined thereafter. Achievement = (60–59)/(90–59)=3% (both phases).

title.narrative: IRI 7 - Number of people screened and diagnosed with diabetes

comment.narrative: IRI 7 was an original indicator with a BL of 1682 and a T of 8000. The T was increased twice to reach 13,500 in the June 2023 restructuring. The BL was updated to 6,740 in line with updated CMIS data. The BL, T, and reported numbers represent the # of people with a diagnosis of diabetes seen for any reason at outpatient departments in facilities connected to CMIS during year Y. This indicator does not represent screening (which is for patients not yet diagnosed) or new diagnosis (since both existing and new diabetes patients are included). Although the numbers therefore do not correspond to the original indicator label ("# of people screened and diagnosed with diabetes"), they are a useful gauge of ongoing access to primary health care services for patients with diabetes. The IRI 7 achievement rate is (16,563-6,740)/(13,500-6,740) = 145 % for both phases.

title.narrative: PDOI 3 - Percentage of adolescents served or reached with quality sexual and reproductive health services

comment.narrative: Original: BL=0, T=70, 22 facilities. T reduced to 60 (2022 restr.) and 5 facilities(Ntfonjeni, Siteki, Mahlangatsha, Mafutseni, Siphofaneni), 50 (2023 restr.), and 20 (2025 restr.). Numer. services include HIV testing, antiretroviral therapy, ANC, postnatal care & family planning. 2023 restr. defines denom. as size of the age 10–19 cohort for the 5 sites, fixed at 17,896 in all years based on 2021 data & assuming equal cohort entry/exit; national cohort size is ~277,000. June 2022 restr. cites “Mobisite” as data source but actual is CMIS. ISR value (24) used cumulative numer. with annual denom., though PAD, RPs, & project docs do not specify cumulative numer. The final T=20 also implies numer. was intended to be annual. ICR recalculated BL (6.5) & end value (7.5) from CMIS using annual numer. and denom. Indicator was not achieved in either phase regardless of choice of T or # of facilities. Achievement = (7.5–6.5)/(60–6.5)=2% (Phase I) and (7.5–6.5)/(20–6.5)=7% (Phase II).

title.narrative: IRI 5 - Percentage of women receiving post-partum check-up within 14 days

comment.narrative: IRI 5 is an original indicator that had a baseline of 84.7 and target of 90. The June 2022 restructuring updated the baseline and target to 60 and 80 respectively, based on CMIS data. In June 2023, the target was increased to 90 because the target of 80 was achieved in 2022. The ICR recalculated the numerator based on CMIS, and found an achievement of 80 in 2022 and a final achievement of 74 in 2025. The source of data is CMIS for the numerator and statistical data for the denominator.The IRI 5 achievement rate is (90-74)/(90-60) = 47% for both phases.

title.narrative: IRI 10 - Proportion of health facilities using CMIS for routine reporting

comment.narrative: IRI 10 was an original indicator with a baseline of 75 and a target of 80. In the June 2022 restructuring, the baseline was modified to 54 to align it with updated CMIS data. The denominator for this IRI is 327 facilities, including 272 primary care facilities. At the time of the ICR, data showed that CMIS coverage increased from 210 facilities in 2020 to 260 in 2025, representing a rise from 64 to 76 percent. The ICR therefore uses a baseline of 64 rather than 54. The IRI 10 achievement rate is (76-64)/(80-64) = 75% for both phases.
